concepts.name: Malay Archipelago
concepts.definition: World's largest archipelago, over 25,000 islands between mainland Southeast Asia and Australia, spanning Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and neighbours.

concepts.name: British Isles
concepts.definition: Archipelago in the North Atlantic off northwestern Europe, comprising Great Britain, Ireland and over 6,000 smaller islands across two states, the UK and Ireland.

concepts.name: Japanese archipelago
concepts.definition: Chain of over 14,000 islands off the Pacific coast of East Asia forming the state of Japan, stretching some 3,000 km; its five largest islands are Hokkaido, Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu and Okinawa.

concepts.name: Aleutian Islands
concepts.definition: Volcanic island chain arcing about 1,900 km from Alaska toward Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula, separating the Bering Sea from the Pacific Ocean and forming part of the Ring of Fire.

concepts.name: Kuril Islands
concepts.definition: Russian-administered volcanic archipelago of 56 islands stretching about 1,300 km between Japan's Hokkaido and Kamchatka, dividing the Sea of Okhotsk from the Pacific; its southern islands are disputed by Japan.

concepts.name: Canary Islands
concepts.definition: Spanish volcanic archipelago in the Atlantic about 100 km off northwest Africa, comprising seven main islands including Tenerife, home to Spain's highest peak, Mount Teide.

concepts.name: Balearic Islands
concepts.definition: Spanish archipelago in the western Mediterranean off eastern Iberia, comprising Mallorca, Menorca, Ibiza and Formentera.

concepts.name: Greater Antilles
concepts.definition: The larger islands of the Caribbean, comprising Cuba, Hispaniola, Jamaica and Puerto Rico, making up nearly 90% of the West Indies' landmass.

concepts.name: Lesser Antilles
concepts.definition: Arc of smaller Caribbean islands running from near Puerto Rico southeast toward South America, forming the eastern edge of the West Indies.
